subject: physics
question_text: Define viscosity. Give its units and dimensional formula.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Mechanical Properties of Fluids, Very Short Answer Question 11, starred as a repeated question (printed p.106). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: viscosity is the property by which a fluid opposes relative motion between its layers, measured by the coefficient of viscosity η = F/(A·dv/dx), the shearing stress divided by the rate of strain; SI unit N s m⁻² (pascal second), CGS unit poise (1 Pa s = 10 poise), dimensional formula [ML⁻¹T⁻¹] — confirmed from F = ηA(dv/dx) ⇒ η = [MLT⁻²]/([L²][T⁻¹]) = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Give the definition — the property by which a fluid opposes relative motion between its own layers; the comparison with friction helps but the definition alone is the answer.
steps.why: The friction analogy makes the definition concrete: a faster layer drags a slower one forward and is dragged back in turn, exactly as friction acts between two solid surfaces.
common_mistakes: Defining viscosity as a fluid's thickness. Thickness is not a physics definition.
Leaving out that it acts between the fluid's own layers.

recall.must_convey: That viscosity is the property by which a fluid opposes relative motion between its layers, the analogue of friction between solids.

steps.memory_tip: Viscosity is friction, but between layers of the same fluid.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give η's formula, then its SI unit and dimensional formula.
steps.why: The formula shows η as stress over strain rate, which is exactly what fixes its unit N s m⁻² and its dimensional formula [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].
common_mistakes: Naming only the SI unit and leaving out the dimensional formula, or the reverse — the question asks for both.
Writing the unit as N s⁻¹ m⁻² instead of N s m⁻².
